content: We need to indicate number of C=O groups in the molecule. We need the molecule structure. Not provided directly. We have tools: IR spectra, carbon NMR, proton NMR, HSQC. To count carbonyl groups, easiest is IR: look for C=O stretch ~1700 cm-1. Could also use carbon NMR: carbonyl carbons appear ~190-220 ppm. But we need the molecule; maybe the system has a sample at hand (some unknown). We need to measure something. Since we don't know the molecule, we need to get data. Use IR spectra first (cheapest?). Probably IR is cheap. Use ir_spectra tool.
